name: Long Island: The Hamptons & Montauk
summary: The island's East End — surf and a historic lighthouse at Montauk, moneyed villages in the Hamptons, and wine country on the North Fork.

lodging.name: A Montauk motel or Hamptons inn
lodging.blurb: Montauk for a laid-back beach base; the Hamptons for village charm.

foodMustTry.name: A Montauk lobster roll & fresh oysters
foodMustTry.blurb: Off the docks at the End — plus North Fork oysters.

days.label: Day 85 — Montauk & the End
days.summary: Surf beaches and the oldest lighthouse in New York.

item.title: Montauk Point Lighthouse
item.blurb: Commissioned by George Washington in 1792 — the oldest lighthouse in the state, at the island's very tip.

item.title: Ditch Plains Beach
item.blurb: Montauk's famous surf break and a laid-back beach afternoon.

days.label: Day 86 — The Hamptons & North Fork wine
days.summary: Village strolls and a wine-country afternoon.

item.title: East Hampton & Sag Harbor
item.blurb: East Hampton's hedges and boutiques, then the old whaling port of Sag Harbor.

item.title: North Fork wineries
item.blurb: Tasting rooms among the vineyards of the quieter North Fork.

days.label: Day 87 — Back west & up the Hudson
days.summary: Leave the East End for the Hudson Valley.

commute.scenicNote: A long haul back around the city and north up the Hudson.
